final.answer: The item directly upstream of CHV-2-2 is FV-2-2, and its datasheet is for the Fisher ET. "Fisher ET" is not a valve body or trim material type — it is the valve model/family name (Fisher™ ET, EAT and ETR Sliding-Stem Control Valves, part of the easy-e™ family). Tool result:
Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [4, 3, 22, 2, 21, 7, 28, 25]:
Yes — the valve is a Fisher ET (that is the valve/trim family name used throughout the datasheet). "Fisher ET" is the valve family, not a body/trim material type. What it is:

- **Product**: The document is titled "Fisher™ ET, EAT and ETR Sliding-Stem Control Valves" [p. 1]. The ET is a single-port, globe-style control valve with cage guiding, a balanced valve plug, and push-down-to-close plug action [p. 3].
- **Valve sizes**: NPS 1, 1-1/2, 2, 2-1/2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 (sizes listed individually in the facts, e.g. valve size 1, 1-1/2, 2-1/2, 3, 6, 8, 8; approximate weights by size in Table 1) [pp. 3–4].
- **Function**: For throttling or on/off control of a wide variety of liquids and gases [p. 2].
- **Family**: The ET, EAT and ETR belong to the easy-e™ family of Fisher industrial control valves [p. 2]. The EAT is the angle version of the ET (self-draining, easier piping), and the ETR is like the ET but push-down-to-open [p. 3].
- **Body materials**: Cast iron, WCC or LCC carbon steel, WC9 chrome moly steel, CF8M (cast 316 stainless), CF3M (cast 316L stainless) or other materials on request [p. 3].
- **Flow direction (ET)**: Normally down with a Standard Cage or Standard Cage with Liner for Metal Seat; always down with a Cavitrol cage; always up with Whisper Trim and WhisperFlo cages [p. 4].

Note: the datasheet covers the ET, EAT and ETR together; if you need to know whether a particular valve on site is the ET (rather than EAT/ETR), check the variant marking — the datasheet does not describe how to identify the variant on the nameplate.

final.answer: The item directly downstream of E-2-1 is FV-2-2. Its datasheet (Fisher ET/D100022X012) lists the following seal/plug seal materials and temperature limits: 2-piece valve plug seal — carbon-filled PTFE (−73 to 232 °C / −100 to 450 °F), ethylene-propylene (−40 to 232 °C / −40 to 450 °F; for hot water/steam, not hydrocarbons), fluorocarbon (−18 to 204 °C / 0 to 400 °F; for air/hydrocarbons, not steam or ammonia), nitrile (−40 to 71 °C / −40 to 160 °F for air and hydrocarbons, or −40 to 82 °C / −40 to 180 °F for other fluids). Spring-loaded valve plug seal — PTFE with N10276 spring (−73 to 232 °C / −100 to 450 °F), PTFE/graphite with R30003 spring (−73 to 316 °C / −100 to 600 °F in non-oxidizing service, up to 260 °C / 500 °F in oxidizing), and PEEK (temperature limits not listed). Above 232 °C / 450 °F, PEEK anti-extrusion rings with a spring-loaded seal ring are required. No separate 'piston ring' part with temperature ratings is given in the datasheet.

final.answer: GV-1-2 is a GF PS servo-controlled 2/2-way solenoid diaphragm valve (circuit function A, failsafe closed, PN6). The datasheet contains no troubleshooting section, so no definitive fault can be confirmed from the documents. However, the specifications suggest the most likely causes: (1) This is a servo-controlled (pilot-operated) diaphragm valve that requires a minimum differential pressure of 0.5 bar between inlet and outlet to open — if the differential pressure across the valve is below 0.5 bar, it will not open even though the coil is energized (the humming you hear). (2) A humming coil can also indicate an electrical supply problem: the datasheet specifies supply voltages of 24V DC, 230V 50/60Hz or 115V 50/60Hz with ±10% tolerance, and warns of component failure risk on AC-powered valves — check that the applied voltage and current type match the type plate. Additional checks within spec limits: medium temperature 0–50 °C, ambient 0–40 °C (PVC housing), and the medium must be clean liquid without solid particles at ≤21 mm²/s viscosity — debris or media outside these limits could also impede the servo diaphragm. The datasheet requires any maintenance be done by authorized specialists per the installation manual (www.gfps.com/is-manuals-valves), and notes the valve has a manual override that could be used to operate it manually while troubleshooting.

final.answer: PV-2-1 is a globe-style control valve (Fisher ET/EAT type per its datasheet). In this design the shutoff when closed is made at the seat: for metal-seat construction the plug closes against the seat ring, and for the standard PTFE (soft) seat construction the seal is a PTFE disk/disk-seat assembly at the seat; the valve plug seal is a separate seal that bears against the cage (balancing the plug) and is not the primary shutoff element — except on TSO (tight shutoff) trim, where the protected soft seat plus plug seal provide Class V shutoff. So a leak-through when shut is most likely at the seat ring/soft seat (e.g., worn PTFE disk, damaged seat surface, or insufficient seat load), not the plug seal. The datasheet does not contain a field inspection/leak-check procedure — the only leakage check mentioned is the factory test (TSO trim: no leakage at shipment, water as test medium; shutoff classes per ANSI/FCI 70-2 / IEC 60534-4, Class IV standard for metal seat, Class V/VI optional). To check, you would isolate the valve, pressurize upstream, and observe downstream leakage, then inspect the seat ring/PTFE disk and plug seal ring at overhaul — but the specific step-by-step procedure is not in the documents.

{"tool": "datasheet", "tag": "PV-2-1", "question": "What type of valve is PV-2-1 (seat/plug design, sealing mechanism), and what does the datasheet say about leakage when closed, seat ring vs plug seal, and how to inspect or check for leakage?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [2, 6, 13, 29, 7, 27, 24, 18]:
**Short answer:** The datasheet you are searching (Fisher ET / EAT / ETR, document fisher-et-d100022x012) does not use the identifier "PV‑2‑1", so I cannot confirm that this name belongs to the valve described. What the datasheet does describe is a single-port, globe-style control valve with **cage guiding, a balanced valve plug, and push-down-to-close action** [p. 3, Table 1. Specifications]. If PV‑2‑1 is your site's name for this valve, read on; if it is a different product, these facts do not cover it.

**Type and sealing mechanism**
- Seating is **metal-to-PTFE seating as standard** in all valves except those with Cavitrol III cages (this is used for stringent shutoff requirements). **Metal-to-metal seating is optional** for all other valves, and is the **standard** for valves with Cavitrol III cages (for higher temperatures) [p. 2, General Application].
- The shutoff/sealing is done at the **valve plug seal**: a backup ring or spring loading forces the valve plug seal ring **against the cage** (see Figure 3 on page 3) [p. 3, Features].
- Two plug-seal constructions exist in the parts list [p. 20]:
  - **2-piece valve plug seal** – standard for NPS 1 through 6 valves, except those with a Cavitrol III cage (materials include nitrile, carbon-filled PTFE).
  - **Spring-loaded valve plug seal** – also used, and required for applications using PEEK anti-extrusion rings (PEEK = a hard plastic used as anti-extrusion rings at high temperature; with these plus a spring-loaded PTFE seal the temperature limit extends to 232 °C / 450 °F, and to 316 °C / 600 °F in non-oxidizing service) [p. 2, p. 20].
- A sectional drawing on page 8 shows the seal ring, retaining ring and metal backup ring of the plug seal (NPS 1–4 ET / NPS 1–6 EAT, and NPS 6 or 8 ET versions).

**Leakage when closed (shutoff classes, Table 4 on p. 6, per ANSI/FCI 70-2 and IEC 60534-4)**
- **Class IV is the standard** shutoff class for metal seating (all constructions shown).
- **Class V and Class VI are optional**:
  - Metal seating: Class V optional (it requires a spring-loaded seal ring, radius-seat plug and wide-bevel seat ring; not available with the 8-in. port quick-opening cage, nor with trims 4, 29 and 85). Class VI optional per Table 6.
  - PTFE seating: Class V (standard), Class V Air Test, and Class VI optional.
- **TSO (Tight Shutoff) trim** (ET/EAT, CL125 through 600): TSO is *not* an ANSI/FCI leakage class. Valves with TSO trim are **factory tested to a more stringent Emerson requirement of no leakage at time of shipment; the test medium is water**. Shutoff class V. Specify service P when ordering [p. 6].
- **Seat type for Class VI (Table 6, p. 7):** available for both Soft seat and Metal seat, port sizes about 3.4375 to 7 in.; minimum seat load for metal seat is **300 lbs/lineal inch**; for soft seat, see Catalog 14; not for use with NPS 8; limited retrofit capability – consult Emerson.

**Seat ring vs plug seal**
- For **metal seat construction**, the closing seal is at the **seat ring**, whose material depends on the trim (for example S41600, R30006, S31600/CoCr-A seat, S31803/Ultimet – see Table 12 on pages 13–14 and Table 23 on p. 27).
- For **PTFE-seat construction**, the parts are a **disk seat, retainer and PTFE disk** (labels in the Figure 3 sectional drawing, p. 8; e.g. trims 85C/87C are PTFE-seat trims, p. 27).
- The **valve plug seal** (against the cage) is a separate seal from the seat; for the TSO trim, Figure 9 on page 16 is a sectional drawing showing where the **valve plug seal** and the **protected soft seat** sit in the trim.

**Inspecting / checking leakage:** I could not find in these facts any inspection or maintenance procedure for checking seat or plug-seal leakage. The only leakage check mentioned is the **factory leak test for TSO trim** (no leakage at shipment, water as test medium) [p. 6].
